fields.sample_size: Single community-managed rural water system (SPAMDes Tirto Sari Ponces, Jambon Village, Nanggulan, Kulon Progo, Yogyakarta; established 2017 with NGO funds; 125 consumers in 2023: 120 houses, 2 mosques, 3 businesses): questionnaire to all 3 managers (8 items) and to 21 consumers (items numbered to 14; how the 21 were chosen is not described, about 17% of the 125 connections), a field survey of infrastructure, interviews and management reports; sustainability scored on four dimensions (managerial, environmental, technical, financial)
fields.effect_measure: descriptive satisfaction percentages and sustainability scores by dimension; no inferential estimate
fields.effect_estimate: Consumer-questionnaire scores (Table 7): managerial 262/372 moderately sustainable, environmental 204/276 moderately sustainable, technical 307/336 highly sustainable, financial 291/360 highly sustainable. Satisfaction: water quality 36% very satisfied, 38% satisfied, 26% quite satisfied; service 62/32/6; information 58/32/10; tariff 62% very satisfied in section 3.5.6 but 40/45/15 in the Conclusion; water quantity 40/45/15 in the text and 45/40/15 in the Conclusion. Average demand 371.6 litres per house per day (about 92.9 litres per person); tariff IDR 2,500 per m3 against an operating cost of IDR 3,000; new connection fee about IDR 600,000-700,000. The system has no written operating procedures, managers meet unscheduled and consumers once a year; it receives no government funding; infrastructure is not well maintained (a reservoir near a goat farm). The paper's own tables do not reconcile (Table 6 gives managerial 226, environmental 195 and technical 292 against 262, 204 and 307 in Table 7).
fields.section: Full text (conference paper, 12 pages): 1 Background; 2 Research method (location, data collection, sustainability scoring); 3 Results and discussion (infrastructure, manager and customer questionnaires, total scores, comparison with three other SPAMDes); Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Tables 1-3 (consumers, infrastructure, manager questionnaire); Tables 4-7 (customer questionnaire, dimension scores, sustainability levels); Table 10 (comparison with three other SPAMDes); Conclusion
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: MMAT (re-appraised 2026-10-09 on the full text; supersedes the abstract-only rating). S1=Yes; S2=Yes. Mixed-methods criteria: 5.1(rationale)=Can't tell (no explicit rationale for combining questionnaires, field survey and interviews); 5.2(integration)=Can't tell (manager and customer scores are combined into dimension scores, interviews are used as 'additional data' without a described procedure); 5.3(meta-inference)=Can't tell; 5.4(divergence)=Can't tell (the comparison with three other systems is descriptive; internal discrepancies are not discussed); 5.5(component quality)=No (21 consumers with no stated selection, the scoring formula is garbled, and table and text figures conflict: Table 6 versus Table 7 totals, tariff and water-quantity percentages). Per MMAT's own guide, no composite score is computed.

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a descriptive mixed-methods case study of one community-managed rural water system in Indonesia (questionnaires to 3 managers and 21 consumers, field survey); read in full text 2026-10-09.
